newsitem.title: KENYA: IFC/Mitsubishi to ease Tanzania office shortage.
newsitem.headline: IFC/Mitsubishi to ease Tanzania office shortage.

text.p: Tanzania's severe shortage of modern office buildings will be eased by plans to build a new office complex in the capital Dar es Salaam.
The International Finance Corporation (IFC) and Mitsubishi Corporation have approved investments of $4.05 million in the $9 million complex, the IFC said in a statement in Nairobi on Monday.
IFC and Mitsubishi will invest $2.25 million and $1.8 million respectively in International House.
The project will also fund rehabilitation of the Dar es Salaam Botanical Garden, a public park adjacent to the site, IFC said.
"The project will help remedy the lack of financing that has hindered the development of modern business infrastructure in Tanzania," said IFC official Tei Mante.

"By demonstrating how private sector investment in the real estate sector can be profitable, International House will hopefully encourage other companies to look at opportunities in the country," Mante added.

IFC's investment consists of a loan of $1.65 million and an equity investment of $600,000. International House will be owned by Mitsubishi Corporation, Konoike Construction of Japan, Murray & Roberts Investments Ltd of South Africa and Tanzania Telecommunications Company Ltd.
IFC did not say when the investments were approved or where the balance of funding would come from. It gave no indication of when construction work on International House would begin.
IFC, a member of the World Bank Group, is the largest multilateral source of equity and loan financing for private sector projects in developing countries.
The project is Mitsubishi's first investment in Tanzania.
